feather.types: Filling feathers are graded by species (goose or duck), size and curl. Small, curved body feathers give springier fill than flat or large feathers, and whole feathers are preferred over crushed or chopped ones. Feather fills are sold as blends labeled by composition: a pillow may be mostly feathers with a small share of down, stated for example as 95 percent feathers and 5 percent down. In US industry practice, blends with less than 75 percent down cluster must list both down and feather percentages. Decorative feathers form a separate trade, graded by species, length and color, and many wild species are legally protected.
feather.fabrics: Feathers and feather-rich blends fill pillows, sofa and seat cushions, featherbeds (mattress toppers) and budget comforters. Their spring suits cushions that must support weight rather than simply insulate. Casings use tightly woven, down-proof cotton ticking to stop quills from escaping. Decorative uses include millinery, costume, fly-fishing flies, trims and fans. Industrial poultry feathers, a far larger stream, are hydrolyzed into feather meal or researched as a keratin source for films, fibers and composites.
feather.quality: Squeeze a feather pillow: it should rebound readily and feel resilient rather than flat or crunchy. Many sharp quills poking through suggest large feathers or thin ticking. Check the label for species and the down and feather percentages, and look for disclosure of crushed feathers, which the FTC says must be stated when more than minimal. A clean, neutral smell indicates well-washed fill. Tight, down-proof ticking with a high thread density lasts longer. For decorative feathers, ask about species and legal origin, since trade in feathers of many wild birds is restricted.
pros: Curved feathers give firm, springy support that suits cushions and pillows.
Feather fill is cheaper than down and makes use of an abundant by-product.
Feather bedding has been found to accumulate less dust-mite allergen than some synthetic bedding.
Feather fillings can be washed, re-sorted and reused.
cons: Quills can poke through casings and prick the user.
Feathers insulate less than down per unit weight.
Fillings flatten over time and need regular plumping.
Wet feathers mat, dry slowly and can develop odor or mildew.
feather.impact: Filling feathers are a by-product of duck and goose meat production and share the welfare issues of down, including live plucking in some regions, which standards such as the Responsible Down Standard also cover because they apply to feathers. Processing uses water, detergent and heat for washing and sanitizing. The much larger chicken feather stream is often a disposal problem, and converting it to keratin materials is an active research area. For health, New Zealand studies from 1999 and 2002 measured markedly lower house dust mite allergen (Der p 1) in feather pillows than in synthetic ones, which a 2004 study linked mainly to the tighter weave of feather pillow covers.
feather.care: Plump feather pillows and cushions daily to redistribute the fill. Use a removable, washable protector and wash that often. Wash feather pillows only when needed, in a front-loading machine on a gentle cycle, about 30 C or as labeled, with a mild or down detergent, two at a time for balance. Dry thoroughly on low heat with dryer balls, checking that no damp clumps remain, since damp feathers mildew. Air in sunlight to freshen. Replace pillows when they no longer recover after plumping. Store decorative feathers flat or in boxes away from light, dust and pests. The product label governs.
faq: What is the difference between a feather pillow and a down pillow?

Feathers have a stiff central quill and give firmer, springier support; down clusters have no quill and give soft, light loft. Many pillows blend both, and the label must state the percentages when down is less than 75 percent in US practice.
Are feather pillows bad for dust mite allergies?

Not necessarily. New Zealand studies found lower dust-mite allergen in feather pillows than in synthetic pillows, largely because feather pillow covers are woven more tightly. Allergen-proof covers help with any pillow type.
Why do feathers poke out of my pillow?

Stiff quills work through gaps between the threads of the casing. Large or broken feathers and loosely woven ticking make it worse. A tightly woven, down-proof pillow protector reduces it, and pulling a quill out backward avoids enlarging the hole.
How often should a feather pillow be replaced?
When it stays flat after plumping or smells even after washing. A folding test helps: fold the pillow in half; if it does not spring open, the fill has lost resilience.
notable: A 1999 New Zealand study found new synthetic pillows accumulated about three times as much dust-mite allergen as new feather pillows over 12 months.
In lab tests, live dust mites passed through standard synthetic pillow covers within 24 hours but not through feather pillow covers.
The FTC says selling feather products with more than minimal crushed or damaged plumage without disclosure would be deceptive.
